text:
lydia (support): heads-up — multiple customers in eu-west-1 reporting p95 latency jump since ~06:20 UTC. Symptoms: higher TLS handshake time, occasional 504s. Happened after a lull, not correlated to higher traffic on metrics we saw. Raising to eng-sre. @oncall please triage :wave:

aj (eng-runtime): copying here. do we have a cluster/route scope? which model routes are affected? any logs?

lydia (support): mostly API generation endpoints, a couple of embedding requests too. here's one customer repro (redacted):

curl -w "time_namelookup:%{time_namelookup}\ntime_connect:%{time_connect}\ntime_appconnect:%{time_appconnect}\ntime_pretransfer:%{time_pretransfer}\ntime_starttransfer:%{time_starttransfer}\ntime_total:%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\"

output:
time_namelookup:0.012
time_connect:0.084
time_appconnect:0.421
time_pretransfer:0.084
time_starttransfer:0.560
time_total:0.562

note: appconnect ~421ms is TLS handshake time, p95s in our dashboards show ~400ms->700ms for eu-west-1 routes

maria (sre): I pulled edge metrics — TLS handshake latency spike lines up with 06:18–06:30 UTC window. No big CPU/GPU saturation on serving hosts. Egress latencies to upstream auth and billing look normal. This smells like network/edge routing change.

chandler (network): running quick traceroute from the edge to client IP and to upstream loadbalancer. traceroute shows an extra cross-zone hop after the last maintenance window:

traceroute to 35.200.12.34 (35.200.12.34), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.1.1  0.48 ms  0.37 ms  0.39 ms
 2  10.254.3.5  1.12 ms  0.95 ms  1.03 ms
 3  34.250.1.12.eu-west-1  2.21 ms  2.11 ms  2.18 ms
 4  34.250.2.66.eu-west-1  25.44 ms  24.98 ms  25.10 ms

that jump in hop 4 looks like an AZ cross over — 2x extra network traversal. Also saw a BGP reconvergence event in provider logs around 06:15 UTC.

sre-bot: automated alert — route-flap detected in provider eu-west backbone (ID: bgp-5473) at 06:14 UTC. Impacted prefixes: 34.250.0.0/16

aj (eng-runtime): ok if BGP flaps caused ECMP changes we could be getting suboptimal paths. Two immediate mitigation ideas: 1) steer traffic away from the problematic POP/next-hop by adjusting router weights, 2) reduce DNS TTL to force client-side re-resolve to healthier IPs. Thoughts?

chandler (network): agree. we can backoff weight for the affected POP in the smart-router config. making that change should take effect within seconds for new connections. also recommend decreasing Route53 health-check TTL for the affected alias to 30s while we validate.

maria (sre): customers are seeing elevated TLS setup times specifically — could be TLS session resumption rates dropped because of IP churn. if connections land on different edge machines without shared session ticket keys, session resumption fails and full handshake happens. are session ticket keys rotating or replicated?

aj (eng-runtime): session ticket keys are stored in the control plane and pushed to edges on deploy. last deploy was 03:40 UTC. the keyset didn't change at 06:15. but if traffic is hitting different cluster instances across AZs and those instances don't have shared ticket keys (some edge hosts lagging), that would cause full handshakes. check ticket-key propagation status.

chandler (network): also check MTU/fragmentation — we saw an increase in retransmits for TLS records in tcpdump capture. small chance there's a path MTU blackhole causing handshake retransmits and timeout backoffs. here's a 3-line tcpdump sample from an affected edge host:

14:06:22.123456 IP 10.10.1.5.443 > 10.0.4.23.52344: Flags [P.], seq 1234:1789, ack 301, win 64240, length 555
14:06:22.125678 IP 10.10.1.5.443 > 10.0.4.23.52344: Flags [P.], seq 1779:2334, ack 301, win 64240, length 555 (frag reassembly)

chandler (network): retransmits + frag reassembly indicates possible MTU issues between the edge POP and client-facing egress path. i've opened a ticket with provider NOC for the bgp flap and asked them to verify MTU on affected links.

lydia (support): customers requesting ETA and workaround. what's our short-term plan?

aj (eng-runtime): short term: 1) adjust smart-router weights to route new sessions away from the affected POPs, 2) reduce DNS TTL for affected records to 30s, 3) enable forced session ticket re-sync to ensure all edges have same ticket set (one-off push), 4) communicate to customers that we're routing around the problem.

maria (sre): also enable longer TCP keepalives on the edge frontdoor so sessions have higher chance to reuse established connections during transient churn. that reduces new handshake counts. I'll file the kernel sysctl change and roll to edge hosts via canary and monitor.

chandler (network): Provider NOC responded — they confirmed a partial fiber switch and BGP reconvergence. they've restored the primary path but are still seeing higher packet reordering on the affected links. they recommend we keep traffic off that path for now. I've pushed weight changes: smart-router:pop:eu-west-1a -> weight: 0.2 -> was 1.0.

deploy-bot: control-plane change applied by chandler — smart-router weights updated for eu-west-1a at 06:42 UTC (change-id: srw-9921).

aj (eng-runtime): pushed session ticket re-sync to all edge machines at 06:45 — confirmed 100% success via rollout-check. this should improve resumption rates on new connections.

maria (sre): kernel keepalive tweak staged to 5% canary at 06:52. monitoring p95s now.

sre-bot: metric alert cleared: tls-handshake-p95-eu-west-1 at 07:05 UTC (was firing).

lydia (support): customers are reporting improvement, p95 back down to normal ranges for the last 40m. pushing update to the affected cases. thanks team. :tada:

aj (eng-runtime): next steps / action items:
- chandler: follow up with provider NOC to validate MTU and packet reordering fix (INC-8792).
- maria: roll keepalive sysctl to all edges once canary stable and monitor for regressions.
- aj: add short-term DNS TTL change revert automation so we don't forget to restore original TTLs in 24h.
- support: collect two anonymized client traces for deeper analysis if provider claims fix.

chandler (network): filing provider follow-up now. will attach traceroutes and tcpdumps.

maria (sre): i'll create a short postmortem stub and link INC-8792. include root-cause hypothesis: BGP reconvergence + ECMP path change + session-ticket non-uniformity -> increased full TLS handshakes -> p95 regression. mitigation: routing weight steering + ticket re-sync + keepalive.

lydia (support): closing customer escalations after confirmation. thanks again.

aj (eng-runtime): leaving this thread open for a day to verify no recurrence, will close after provider confirms stable path and we revert TTLs.

sre-bot: incident recorded: INC-8792 (networking) — status: monitoring.

chandler (network): quick note — let's add an automation to detect sudden increases in appconnect time (TLS handshake) and correlate with BGP/route-flap signals so we can auto-steer next time. filing automation request (AUT-314).

maria (sre): agreed. good candidate for Redwood Optimize ruleset down the road.

end of thread.
